scope.no_repair: A0 records findings; A1-A7 and the owning ETP items repair them.
scope.rule_cited_not_rederived: Where freshness, closure discipline or the claim algebra already covers a case, the rule identifier is cited and the finding is limited to what the rule does not detect.

class_definitions.truncation: a record reports a bounded population as if it were complete: a top-N without its N, a sample as a census, or an aggregate whose members are absent.
class_definitions.silent_suppression: a finding, failure, skip or unresolved row disappears between a detail record and a summary, including one reclassified rather than resolved.
class_definitions.summary_without_reconstruction: a percentage, verdict or pass that cannot be recomputed from the tracked evidence a reader has.
class_definitions.wrong_candidate_application: evidence produced at one identity used to support a claim at another, including a later artefact used for an earlier claim.

truncation.consequence: An external reader who counts residual_sites concludes the curl closure has 200 unresolved sites and that the remaining population is closed. The record's own blocking predicate is 449 with 219 target-bounded, which is the population element 7 fails on.

The closure record itself carries neither the failing row nor the bound, and closure_discipline.py does not read residual_sites length against totals.reachable_unresolved_sites.

truncation.title: 1,999 lint suppressions are recorded only as per-lint totals
truncation.observed: suppressions carries a total and a by_lint count map (dead_code 703, non_snake_case 460, clippy::too_many_arguments 240, and so on) plus a test-module list. There is no member row for any of the 1,999 suppressions, so the site of a suppression cannot be read from the record.

truncation.title: External package verifies 1,633 selected inputs with no denominator for the evidence tree
truncation.observed: The 56 selection paths include `evidence/etp0`, `evidence/etp`, `evidence/etp2`, `evidence/etp3`, `evidence/etp4` and `evidence/etp5`, but not `evidence/etp-t1` … `evidence/etp-t15`, not `evidence/etp6`, not `evidence/etp7`, not the top-level `evidence/closure-*.json`, and not `forensics/downstream/*atlas*.json`. wrong_candidate_application.title: A discharged obligation asserts a later document state while its evidence digest resolves to the earlier bytes with the opposite value
wrong_candidate_application.observed: OBL-GAP-005 is DISCHARGED with `settled_by: ETP-T15: CAMPAIGN-STATUS.json now records 0/33 section 7 and 1 risk-accepted family`. EV-01 in the same claim records sha256 abb8a6cb… with digest_identity `S`. Hashing `forensics/memory-safety/campaign/safe-c33/CAMPAIGN-STATUS.json` at S=9372bb28b gives abb8a6cb…, and that blob records `consumers.safe_compatible: 1`. The live file is 8affeac4… and records 0.
wrong_candidate_application.expected: the settlement cites evidence at the identity it describes, or the claim declares a source identity that includes the post-S settlement.
wrong_candidate_application.consequence: The discharge looks supported to a reader who trusts the `settled_by` text and false to a reader who re-derives the cited digest. This is the record pattern that ETP-T15 exists to prevent, one level down: the reconciliation is real, but the claim's evidence pointer still names the contradicted bytes. Every claim in the set shares `source_identity.commit=9372bb28b` while five verdicts are settled by a later item.
wrong_candidate_application.existing_coverage: etp_claims.py re-derives every evidence digest at S (80 of 81 match; the one exception is the deliberately withdrawn O7 digest, recorded as a refusal in ETP-5 R3) and therefore cannot see this defect: the digest is correct for S. freshness.py models the claim set as a dependent of S but not the settlement's identity.

wrong_candidate_application.title: The release gate's package item does not bind the package to the candidate under release
wrong_candidate_application.observed: check_package resolves the package root, runs `verify.sh` or `etp6_verify.py`, and reports the verifier's RESULT. It never reads `MANIFEST.json candidate.commit`/`tree` and never compares it with the `--candidate` the gate resolved. A package built from commit 98c7b5d29 therefore satisfies gate-5 for a release at e0b727d06.
wrong_candidate_application.expected: gate-5 refuses `RG_PACKAGE` when the package's candidate commit or tree differs from the candidate the gate resolved, or records the package candidate as an explicit, separate identity in the decision output.
wrong_candidate_application.consequence: A passing release gate can be evidenced by reproduction of a different commit. This is the exact `wrong-candidate application` class the release policy exists to refuse, in the tool that enforces it.
wrong_candidate_application.existing_coverage: the gate's docstring (lines 74-80) disclaims that the package was produced by an independent party and that the claim is true; it does not disclaim, and does not check, package-to-candidate identity. gate-1 binds the gate to HEAD and is unrelated to the package.

wrong_candidate_application.title: The reproducibility record has no committed candidate identity and its post-commit rebuild is NOT_RUN
wrong_candidate_application.observed: The record that carries the byte-identical build result has no `candidate.commit`. The only identity is `head_at_start` plus crate-input tree hashes, and the rebuild of the committed candidate is recorded NOT_RUN. The `identity_status` still says pending although S' was committed before the candidate under audit existed.
wrong_candidate_application.expected: after the commit, `candidate.commit` names it and the post-commit rebuild is either run or explicitly deferred with the gate that will run it.
wrong_candidate_application.consequence: A reader who consumes `candidate.commit` gets null and cannot bind the byte-identical archive to any commit. A reader who consumes the ETP-2 row in the queue gets `S' = e9d492b0d`, which is correct but not present in the record's identity field.
wrong_candidate_application.existing_coverage: the record names `head_at_start`, the recipe digest and the three artefact digests, so the measurement is reconstructable by re-running the tracked recipe; §22 requires the freeze identity in the record and this record predates the post-commit step.

wrong_candidate_application.title: The tracked external-package record describes a different commit from the candidate under audit
wrong_candidate_application.observed: The manifest names candidate 98c7b5d29. At this candidate the ETP-T12 clean-checkout run records `manifest FAIL … the staged tree does not match the frozen manifest. (56 hard refusal(s) against evidence/etp6/MANIFEST.json at this commit)`.
wrong_candidate_application.expected: the package record is regenerated at the candidate it is offered for, or its stale identity is surfaced by gate-5 rather than only by `verify manifest`.
wrong_candidate_application.consequence: The tree's only external-reproduction record is not of the tree. A reader taking `evidence/etp6/MANIFEST.json` as the candidate's external-reproduction evidence is reading another commit's selection and digests.
wrong_candidate_application.existing_coverage: verify.py manifest refuses at this commit (recorded in ETP-T12); release_gate.py gate-5 does not (A0-F16).

ranking.why: It is the only finding where a discharged obligation and its own cited evidence record opposite values. Trusting it: an external reader re-deriving the digest concludes the claim set is internally unsound; trusting the settled_by text without re-deriving concludes a contradiction was resolved on evidence that does not show it. Both readings are wrong, and the defect is in the record that adjudicates every other claim.

It is a live, cited, load-bearing population. Trusting it: a reader counts 200 unresolved sites, finds them contract-bounded, and concludes the curl element-7 blocker is nearly closed. The record's own total is 449 with 219 target-bounded, which is the population that keeps element 7 FAIL and the curl graduation open.

It is the only recorded full release-gate refusal. Trusting it: a reader concludes the gate still refuses four contradictions at this tree and that nothing changed, or that reclassifying the claims removed the refusals without resolution. The current gate produces neither output, and no record binds the receipt to the claim-set bytes it read.

sound.why: 1,633 inputs each carry a path and SHA-256, the selection is a 56-path git-archive list, and five refusals name the paths a selected record cites but the commit does not contain. A missing or altered input fails verification with both hashes named (ETP-T6 mutation controls).

Population, identity, dependency edges and exclusions are derived from the artefacts and the claim/traceability graphs; 228 exclusions are named with reasons, 189 of them by an explicit 512 KiB bound; an unresolved dependency is never UNAFFECTED, and carry-forward must be an explicit HISTORY declaration.

Every node carries a bound_commit and a digest read at that commit, the graph declares its 43 orphans by class with a reason, and the seed reproduces the committed graph byte for byte. The hazard-register projection digest in the graph matches the live HAZARDS.json.

All 81 evidence digests reconstruct: 80 re-derive from the Git blob at S, and the single exception is the withdrawn O7 revision tagged `digest_identity: historical`, which re-derives from the commit cc2e5fa32 named in its note (2ee7ee4d…). The 81st is therefore preserved history, not absent evidence.

Eleven instruments each carry intended use, failure modes, soundness limits and a paired control. Nine controls are executable and re-run; two are RECORDED and bound to a tracked runner digest. A RECORDED control presented as PASS is refused by gate-4.

Every count is derived from a named harness log under stated rules, the log digest and byte length are recorded, and check_receipts.py R4/R5 recompute both. The two skip dialects and the third `Skipped:` spelling are handled by refusing to guess rather than by hand-correcting a row.

Admission is conservative: 0 SATISFIED, 19 REFUSED, 59 NOT_RUN; every REFUSED row names the missing identity fields, and a BLOCKED row without a bound resolves to REFUSED. The defect at A0-F09 is in the separate declaration file, not in this aggregate.

Eight aggregates are audited against their own blocked rows; two are refused with `CD_AGGREGATE_PASS_HIDES_BLOCKED_ROW`. The 1,121 exclusion rows are never dropped: a row missing any of the five requirements is counted as failing, and an incomplete residual sample adds a failing row for the remainder.

The superseded and live bytes of six documents are both preserved with digests, the graduation's original bytes are kept, the dissent is retained unchanged, and the ledger's 1/33 value survives in a history block. A correction preserves what was believed.

The gate-to-article mapping is explicit about its own limits and names the four articles no gate item covers (5, 6, 7, 9). A reader cannot mistake gate coverage for constitution coverage of those four.

All 50 assignments are reported as having a same-party adjudicator and zero external trust domains; the b85c independence claim is refused on four named grounds. The adverse result is recorded rather than smoothed.

limits: Whether the 200 residual_sites rows are a prefix, a sample or the full contract-bounded subclass of the 449 cannot be determined from the record; determining it requires re-running consumer_closure.py, which A0 did not do.
The validity of the 301 carried-forward atlas families at the superseded identity (libcrypto 26ba36ff…) cannot be established here: the prior run record is not in the tree.
The freshness status of the 228 excluded artefacts, including artifacts/phase24/COURTS.json and the five phase25 court records, is unknown; they are excluded from the model by size, not analysed.

Whether HAZ-15 and HAZ-16 changed barrier state deliberately cannot be established from the register: only file mtimes (HAZARDS.json 22:44, RECEIPT.md 10:30) and the queue-row narrative show the order. No transition field exists.
The ETP-7 gate transcript cannot be re-derived without re-running release_gate.py against the preserved pre-reconciliation claim set; A0 did not execute the release gate.
External independence and external reproduction cannot be assessed: no external reviewer or reproducer identity exists, and the ETP-6 status is EXTERNAL_REVIEW_PENDING.
